content.text: For Nigerian creators who rely on Stripe for [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/digital-product-payment-solutions-west-africa-minimum-viable-2|digital]] product sales, a harsh reality sets in when they discover Stripe's absence in their country. The honest answer is that Stripe operates in 46 countries out of 195 on earth, leaving a significant number of creators without access to its services. This infrastructure problem is not limited to Nigeria, but it affects creators in numerous other countries, including Ghana, Kenya, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Venezuela, Zimbabwe, Cameroon, Tanzania, and the Philippines. The situation becomes even more complex when considering the risks associated with PayPal account suspensions, which can hold funds for up to 180 days with no appeal.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Stripe alternatives

Stripe's decision not to support Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Kenya, Ethiopia, and dozens of other countries is not a technical limitation — it is a business decision driven by correspondent banking requirements, local regulatory compliance costs, and risk modeling. PayPal operates the same way. The practical result is that a creator in Lagos with a real product, a real audience, and a real income goal is blocked at the infrastructure level before any transaction ever occurs. The architecture behind this solution is based on a combination of free and paid tools. It includes GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage, and Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery.
